cells.tense: Care is moving through you right now without gripping anything it is tending.
cells.act: let go of the thing you are gripping
cells.ask: Take something you're still holding that has already finished — work, a person, a worry — and open your hands on it today, deliberately. Let it stand there without your hand over it.
cells.core:
You can give something room to grow and keep your hands off it at the same time. In the fog, you don't force the whole road into view; you take the step that has light on it, and you let what you're tending do its growing. That's rare, and it's working.

What keeps it working is one deliberate letting go. Choose something you've carried past its need — work that's done, a worry you've already worried, a hand you keep over something that can stand alone — and open your hands today, on purpose. Decide what you want to walk away from, and walk. Walking away here isn't loss. It's the same care with less weight in it.
cells.sheetLine: You can hold space without holding on. Keep it that way.

cells.tense: Where care is growing, the ending is held in a fist before it has had a season.
cells.act: picture it a year on, turned out well, and keep the picture
cells.ask: When you catch yourself bracing for how someone or something might fail, hold the well-turned version of it twelve months out in your mind for a minute. Once today, no plan to make it happen.
cells.core:
You're running past the thing you're growing, deciding how it should turn out before it has had a season. Care in you has started arranging the ending. You can feel the worry, and you keep moving toward the person like your hand on the wheel is what keeps them upright.

The way out isn't less care — it's a wider frame. When you catch yourself bracing for how it might fail, hold the good version a year from now in your mind for a minute, and keep it. That's the whole act. No plan, no next move; just hold the grown version for a minute and let today stay unwritten. The grip loosens when you can see the thing grown.
cells.sheetLine: You're steering an outcome that hasn't grown yet. Hold a wider view.

cells.tense: Nothing has been growing here for a while, and the door you keep standing at closed behind you.
cells.act: choose the light to steer by and turn toward it
cells.ask: Put on paper something you actually want — not what would be sensible, what you want — and read it back once. No plan, no step. Just let yourself face it.
cells.core:
Nothing grows here right now, and it isn't because you can't tend things. It's that what you're tending has gone quiet, or the door you keep standing at already closed, so the energy has nowhere to arrive. From inside it looks like needing no one and wanting nothing. From outside, a person can watch something go unasked for.

So don't start by trying to care again — start by naming a direction. Put on paper something you actually want, not what would be sensible, and read it back once, quietly. That's the whole act: pick the light you'd steer by, face it, and let yourself see it without planning the walk. The rest warms as the light gets named.
cells.sheetLine: You're asking for nothing. Put down what you'd steer by.

cells.tense: People lean on you as the one who holds them, and you would not put your own name to it.
cells.act: stop holding what no longer serves
cells.ask: Look at what you're carrying for someone — a situation, a standing role. Find one part of it that no longer needs carrying, and stop holding that part. No announcement. Just set it down once.
cells.core:
Others see you as the one who takes care of things, and you've been running the role without having signed for it. Whatever is being held up for other people, someone has been standing under it — and if asked, you'd say you didn't choose the post. Both can be true at once.

One release makes it visible. Take the thing you're carrying for someone — a situation, a standing role — and find one part of it that no longer needs carrying. Stop holding that part. No announcement, no explanation; set it down once and let what stands there stand. Your arms know what they've been carrying. Empty them of one piece and you'll see the shape you left, which was not yours to keep.
cells.sheetLine: You didn't sign up to carry it. Put one piece down.
